forces.title: Sharp Decline in SME Lending Constrains Non-Bank Financial Institutions
forces.description: SME loans in the UK have almost halved as a share of GDP since 2011, with overall lending to private non-financial corporations by Q3 2025 returning to 1998 levels. This significant contraction in business credit availability and flow directly impacts Non-Bank Financial Institutions (IN070201) which are crucial in providing credit to SMEs and asset-light businesses, limiting their potential for growth and market penetration in the UK.
forces.source_title: The UK Financial Services Sector Has Lost Its Edge—Here’s How to Win It Back

forces.title: Consumer Regulations Impede Access to Financial Products and Services
forces.description: While intended for protection, UK consumer regulations have unintentionally reduced consumer access to certain financial products and investment advice. This creates a key risk for Non-Bank Financial Institutions (IN070201) offering consumer finance, as regulatory hurdles may limit their product development and distribution, increase compliance costs, or restrict the customer base they can effectively serve, thereby hindering market growth and innovation.
forces.source_title: The UK Financial Services Sector Has Lost Its Edge—Here’s How to Win It Back

forces.title: AI-Powered Credit Underwriting to Expand Addressable Lending Market
forces.description: The adoption of AI-driven credit underwriting and more granular AI-powered credit models presents a significant opportunity to expand the addressable lending market in the UK. These technologies can enhance accuracy in default prediction, accelerate time-to-decision, and lower processing costs. This makes lending viable for smaller ticket sizes and asset-light businesses previously deemed uneconomic, directly benefiting Non-Bank Financial Institutions (IN070201) and consumer finance providers by opening new growth avenues.
forces.source_title: The UK Financial Services Sector Has Lost Its Edge—Here’s How to Win It Back

viewpoints.title: UK Financial Services Sector Underperforms, Hampering Wider Economic Growth
viewpoints.description: BCG Global asserts that the UK financial services sector has significantly underperformed over the past 15 years, becoming a drag on national productivity. Key indicators include business lending returning to 1998 levels, SME loans halving as a share of GDP since 2011, declining employment, and lost shareholder value. This challenging environment for the overall financial services sector implies a difficult operating landscape for diversified financial services entities, including non-bank financial institutions and diversified financial conglomerates, impacting their growth prospects and profitability.
viewpoints.source_title: The UK Financial Services Sector Has Lost Its Edge—Here’s How to Win It Back

demand_drivers.description: The substantial decline in SME loans as a share of GDP since 2011 signifies reduced demand or availability of credit for small and medium-sized enterprises, directly impacting potential lending volumes for NBFIs and other credit providers in the UK.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis indicates that SME loans have almost halved as a share of GDP since 2011, reflecting a significant contraction in this market segment within the UK financial services sector. This reduction encompasses lending from both banks and other credit providers, which would include Non-Bank Financial Institutions.
market_sizing.source_title: The UK Financial Services Sector Has Lost Its Edge—Here’s How to Win It Back
